newsitem.title: UK: British Airways busy in two-way business.
newsitem.headline: British Airways busy in two-way business.

text.p: In a slow session in the UK stock options market on Monday, the focus of attention was in British Airways and in Zeneca, dealers said.
British Airways attracted a flurry of two-way business, the biggest deal being from a buyer of 750 January 650 calls at 15p.
The underlying shares firmed as investors pondered the prospects of a European backing for the commercial trading of airport take-off and landing slots.
A successful conclusion with this could ease competition barriers and help British Airways with its plans of a transatlantic alliance with AMR's American Airlines.
By 1502 GMT, shares in British Airways were up 6-1/2p to 601p.
In pharmaceuticals group Zeneca, the main deal came from a buyer of 250 January 1700 calls at various prices around 80p.

Elsewhere, a reverse calendar spread was establshed in brewer and distiller Guinness. This involved buying 100 November 460 puts at 19p and selling 100 February 460 puts at 23p making a net credit of 4p.
The spread will reduce the further the underlying shares move away from 460p by November expiry to help make a profit.
The short puts may still be held after November expiry if the trader believes the underlying shares will stay above 460p between the November and February expiry dates.
